title: English Teacher vs. Great Western Detective
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shin'ichi, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Takagi, Chiba) omitted by convention. Heiji Hattori and Jodie Starling are kept as person nodes despite being recurring franchise characters because this two-parter's entire B-plot (the title itself) is Heiji and Conan investigating whether Jodie is secretly the actress Chris Vineyard / a Black Organization contact -- that thread is load-bearing for this specific episode, not incidental. The old cases/ file already had the correct culprit (Noboru Kawakami / p4, matching s3) and a roughly correct one-line summary of the method, so no culprit reversal to report here -- but it was extremely thin: no Sumiyo Hiraya node (the actual motive source, previously buried in a motive_type string), no locked-room mechanism detail (Kawakami secretly turned Takai's bed to face the balcony-less window, then phoned him and said 'I can't hear ya' to draw him toward it), no physical evidence chain (bent curtain rail, the enlarged photo of Takai clutching the curtain and throwing his phone, the voice-memo recording on that phone), no locations split (condo living room vs. bedroom vs. the street below vs. Jodie's separate unit on the same floor), no real relationships (girlfriend, coworker, in-love-with, school/university seniority), and the whole Heiji/Jodie subplot was dropped entirely. A one-sentence detail the old file also omitted: Kawakami disputes intent-to-kill even after confessing (he says he only meant to disorient Takai, not kill him), which is worth keeping as a circumstance_tag rather than silently resolved. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Curtain rail bent and hooks torn off: a genuine suicide wouldn't grab at the curtain on the way out, so the damage shows Takai fought against falling rather than jumping.
Enlarged photo from Shimoda's camera shows Takai clutching the curtain and throwing his phone as he fell -- the throw was deliberate, not an accidental drop.
Takai's bed normally faces the balcony window but was found facing the window with no balcony beneath it -- reenacting the layout shows someone secretly turned it before he fell.
